sample_unit: questions (rated by 20 rhinologists and 24 nonmedical individuals)

links.outcome: Clarity of ChatGPT patient information as rated by nonmedical laypeople versus society material
links.effect: Nonmedical individuals rated ChatGPT clarity higher than SFORL (8.16 ± 1.16 vs. 6.32 ± 1.33; p < 0.0001); rhinologists found no clarity difference (7.61 vs 7.53; p = 0.485).
links.quote: Non-medical individuals scored the clarity of ChatGPT significantly higher than that of the SFORL (8.16 ± 1.16 vs. 6.32 ± 1.33; p < 0.0001).

screen.reason: The study evaluates ChatGPT's ability to generate French patient-facing preoperative medical information compared to professional society materials, assessed by rhinologists and laypeople, without testing a specific organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
